summary:
Project Ark is a terraforming initiative proposed by TAS. The goal is to develop sustainable ecological farms to meet food and feed security. The UN has predicted that by 2050 we will consume 70 % more food in comparison to 2007/2008 levels. This means our capture fisheries industry must expand its sustainable catch limit to meet food security. 

To meet the food security goal of Project Ark, TAS has developed a method to help professional, student and citizen scientists analyse data to terraform oceans into sustainable, productive, ecological farms. The method involves utilising the Giovanni data science platform and "Excel Analysis ToolPak." to quantify and identify statistically significant relationships between variables. This can be tailored for a marine region of your choice.

The key oceanic terraforming parameter to maximise is the dependent variable chlorophyll-a concentration. Chlorophyll-a is maximised by optimising the independent variables, Sea Surface Temperature (SST) and nitrates concentration. However, in future, this method will be expanded to include data analysis for DIC and also incident light intensity.

The data anlaysis method includes visual instructions in the methodology section on how to search, extract and download data from Giovanni for analysis on Excel. TAS has assumed that the scientists and students who use this methodology know how to create charts on Excel as a prerequisite.
details:
What does it do or how does it work? 

TAS has developed a method to search, extract, analyse and present data related to maximising a key terraforming parameter: chlorophyll-a concentration in water. 

The process works by searching the Giovanni data science site for relevant data. The data is plotted, then extracted from the data science site, by downloading. After this, the data undergoes regression to identify the relationship between dependent variable chlorophyll-a and the independent variables SST or nitrates. Then, the output regression summary is interpreted to determine if the results are statistically significant or not (p < 0.05). Time series plots of the results or plots of dependent vs. independent variables were also generated to illustrate the results. Plots of the dependent variable vs. the independent variables have also been produced, too.

What benefits does it have? 

The benefit of knowing the relationship between the chlorophyll-a with the SST and nitrates concentration is that the optimal value of SST and nitrates can be determined to maximise the chlorophyll-a concentration. If the chlorophyll-a concentration can be maximised, then this will lead to the maximisation of the total aquatic biomass in the terraformed ocean. Thus, more fish can be captured by fishing vessels, via sustainable, ecological farming methods. This will lead to much greater food, feed and health supplements production. Importantly, we will achieve greater food security, resulting in the greater human carrying capacity of the Earth.

What is the intended impact of the project? 

The impact of this project is to eventually terraform planets, which are currently barren, such as Mars, to create a second home for humanity. 

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project? 

I used the Giovani data science platform to search and extract data. In addition, I used Microsoft Excel for charting and also for regression analysis, by enabling the Analysis ToolPak add-on.

How is your project creative? 

The project is aimed at professional, citizen and student scientists. The project produces an easy to understand method to search, extract, perform regression, analyse and chart variables useful for terraforming the oceans of our planet.

What factors did your team consider? 

I considered the dependent variable chlorophyll-a concentration and the independent variables SST and nitrates concentration. I considered the time limitations of this competition in dictating how I would go about performing the required tasks for the competition. This meant I had to apply time management to ensure that I met the competition requirements on time.
